title: Docker Swarm
definition: Docker's native container orchestration tool. It allows you to cluster multiple Docker hosts together into a single, highly available virtual system, managed with familiar Docker CLI commands.
simpleExplanation: Kubernetes' little brother. It does the exact same job (managing containers across many servers), but it is vastly simpler to set up and uses the exact same `docker-compose.yml` files you already know.
realWorldExample: A small 5-person startup needs to run an app across 3 servers for redundancy, but they don't have the time to learn the massive complexity of Kubernetes. They run `docker swarm init`, and within 10 minutes, they have a fully load-balanced, multi-server cluster.

basic: Is Docker Swarm more or less complex to configure than Kubernetes?
intermediate: Why did the tech industry largely abandon Docker Swarm in favor of Kubernetes?

answers.question: More or less complex?
answers.answer: Vastly less complex. It is built directly into the Docker Engine.

answers.question: Why abandon it?
answers.answer: While Swarm was easy, Kubernetes was backed by Google and offered exponentially more advanced features for massive enterprises (like granular auto-scaling, custom resource definitions, and massive cloud provider integrations). Kubernetes won the 'Orchestration War'.
